questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many driving skills. They slow your reaction time, reduce coordination, lower alertness, and make it hard to concentrate.

questions.question: You must yield to children playing in the streets.
questions.explanation: You must drive with extreme caution where children are present. Slow down near schools, playgrounds, and residential areas.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Only time will sober you up. Your body must eliminate the alcohol naturally. Eating and drinking cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: Which statement about backing on a roadway is true?

options.text: Signal first to warn traffic behind you that you intend to stop.
You do not need to check traffic when backing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal first to warn traffic behind you that you intend to stop.
questions.explanation: Always look behind you to check for traffic before backing up. Only back up where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: What should you do after an accident?

options.text: Protect the area, notify authorities, and care for the injured.
Report the accident the following week.
Go to a convenience store and call your insurance company.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the area, notify authorities, and care for the injured.
questions.explanation: After an accident, stop your vehicle and move it off the road if possible. Help anyone injured, protect the accident scene, call the police, exchange information with other drivers, and report to your insurance company and the DMV.

questions.question: You must stop when approaching a stopped school bus unloading children on a two-lane road.
questions.explanation: Stop for a school bus loading or unloading passengers on any two-lane road, no matter which direction you are traveling. You must also stop when approaching from behind on a four-lane highway.

questions.question: Drivers may not pass a school bus when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, stop before you reach it and stay stopped until the lights turn off. On roads with a median, vehicles on the opposite side do not need to stop.

questions.question: When driving in a travel lane on the roadway:

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you enter the wrong freeway ramp.
Don't stop. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't stop. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep driving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your exit, do not back up. Go to the next exit where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: Which of the following is against the law and can result in fines and/or jail time?
questions.explanation: Speed limits are the absolute maximum speed allowed. Speeding, racing, or assisting in racing on public roads can result in fines and jail time.

questions.question: An intersection has no traffic signs or signals. You arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right. You should:

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
Drive through and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Slow down and let it pass first, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: After drinking several beers, the only way to reduce alcohol's effects is by:
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not speed this up. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guard signals you to go.
Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign means you are near a school. Be alert and stop if children are crossing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A round sign always means a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: What colors are used for signs showing the distance to the next highway exit?
questions.explanation: Signs that show where to go are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal three to four seconds before you turn. This warns other drivers of your move.

questions.question: Drivers should be careful when passing large vehicles and should not drive beside them for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have large blind spots on both sides. Do not stay beside a large vehicle for long. Either drop back or pass quickly.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, you should:

options.text: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Wear both parts of a two-part seat belt. Using only one part gives you much less protection. Even with an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger directs you to stop.
A stop sign controls the crossing.
Flashing red lights and gates are active.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger or stop sign tells you to, or if flashing red lights and gates are working.

questions.question: You should not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses because:

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses well in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more time and distance to stop than small cars. A sudden stop in front of a large vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces alertness, increases reaction time, and greatly reduces coordination.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver is behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as they pass you.
Speed up while they are passing you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If you see an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact with them. Do not speed up—this will only make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: When driving behind a large truck on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Follow closer than you would behind a passenger car.
Follow farther back than you would behind a passenger car.
Drive to the right of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow farther back than you would behind a passenger car.
questions.explanation: Stay farther behind a large truck than you would a passenger car. Trucks have larger blind spots, so you need more distance.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:

options.text: Pull next to them and yell.
Let it go and keep driving safely.
Flash your high beams at them.
Cut them off to get back at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go and keep driving safely.
questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Just let it go and continue driving safely. This helps you avoid road rage.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through as quickly as possible.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Keep your normal speed throughout the zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down and be prepared to stop. Follow posted speed limits and stay alert. Workers may be present.

questions.question: Alcohol is the single greatest common factor in fatal car crashes.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is the number one killer on roadways. It harms your vision and slows your reaction time. Even small amounts of alcohol affect your driving.

questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:

options.text: Talking or texting on a phone.

questions.explanation: You make about 200 decisions for every mile you drive. You need full attention on the road. Any other task can be dangerous.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Check both your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Just before moving, look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: When parallel parking, you should:

options.text: Signal right, pass the space, stop, then back in.
Park within 18 inches of the curb or edge.
Center your vehicle to give other cars room to move.

questions.explanation: Signal right and stop next to the car in front of the space. Back into the space. Park within 18 inches of the curb. Center your car to leave room for other vehicles.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes.

questions.question: Where is it illegal to pass another vehicle?

options.text: At a street crossing or highway intersection

questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills, curves, or where you cannot see far enough ahead. Do not pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, where there are no-passing signs, or where a solid yellow line is on your side. Do not pass if the car ahead stopped for a pedestrian or when in work zones where it is unsafe.
